report:
Reviewed the full atomic_checking claim, all eight associated implementation entries and all five test entries, with the inference design and accepted transaction RFD captured. This is source inspection; no behavioral suites rerun and no source changes made.

The required boundary is all-or-discard inference and staged obligations for a speculative candidate or multipart check, with rejected equalities/wakes/obligations excluded from the requester. The RFD distinguishes exclusive short-lived probes committed to a direct parent from independent candidate proof contexts whose answers cross a canonical boundary. unify.rs try_probe creates a child, runs the entire operation there, rebuilds/collapses only on success and discards on failure; batch unification shares this transaction. egraph.rs collapse_into checks live direct-parent/exclusive-leaf conditions, transfers child maps, revisions and wake effects, reowns variables and removes the child; discard removes branch state. version.rs allocates fresh version nodes, tracks ancestry/liveness and provides the lifecycle restrictions supporting these operations.

infer_ctx.rs commit_branch rebuilds before collapse and publishes resulting wakes afterward. obligations.rs StagedObligationBatch owns unpublished environment/provenance entries; dropping a rejected batch has no registry publication. method.rs stages external inherent receiver and argument matching in a child, discards on mismatch, and commits before publishing the environment. solve/boundary.rs instantiate_query constructs a fresh stash/egraph with newly instantiated canonical inputs, separating proof contexts from requesters. solve/prove.rs prove_conjunction owns a child for the multipart conjunction, discards it on No and commits the resulting state only through its parent boundary on complete or residual outcomes. A residual or Maybe is not misreported here as a rejected No; the caller-facing candidate isolation still depends on the separate proof-context/canonical-result boundary.

The four ordinary tests provide specific evidence. concrete_and_nested_unification asserts a successful tuple relation binds the variable to i32 and merges tuple representatives. late_mismatch_rolls_back_earlier_equality first permits a variable/i32 relation, then fails bool/i32 in the same tuple; it asserts the variable remains its original root and the parent's semantic revision is unchanged. batch_failure_is_atomic similarly fails a later pair and checks the earlier variable binding did not escape. external_method_mismatch_discards_partial_generic_bindings uses the in-file SignatureTcx fixture with owner T, method E and arguments E then bool; passing a caller variable then char fails after partial matching, and assertions check Bound::None plus unchanged root revision. Helpers are visible in the associated files and perform real variable allocation/signature construction rather than opaque verification.

These assertions do not count wake publication or staged-obligation publication, nor do they establish all sibling-candidate identity isolation scenarios. The associated inference_atomic_checking TODO explicitly retains the remaining matrix: partial generic rejection with unchanged parent, corresponding acceptance with exactly one obligation publication, and isolated sibling candidates without shared inference identities. Its prerequisite is completing those targeted observations across the shared transaction callers, including rejection wake/obligation effects required by the claim. The TODO remains non-executable deferred evidence; the successful and failed equality tests are not a blanket proof of the entire speculative checker. All entries and requirements are accounted for, no concrete defect was identified in the inspected paths, and no additional edits are requested.
